resources.string: Offline speech · Transparent overlay · Keep your keyboard
Detects when the keyboard is shown, displays a transparent touch target above the keyboard, and inserts recognition results into the focused field. It does not collect or upload screen content.
e.g. 192.168.1.100:6016 — ws:// and wss:// are also supported
Default port 6016 for CapsWriter-Offline v2.x; use 6006 for older servers.
Starts a low-priority foreground notification and places the transparent target above the keyboard.
May be limited by the system
When enabled, pressing Home does not leave the app in the recent-tasks list. Disable it to switch back from recents. Enabled by default.
Mirrors trash_punc in config_client.py: removes trailing ，。,. from short results. WeChat always strips.
Remove trailing punctuation when the result has at most N semantic units (CJK character / English word / number = 1); longer results keep it. 0 always removes.
Saved under the app-specific Music/CapsWriter folder; no storage permission needed.
Mirrors threshold in config_client.py; shorter presses are treated as accidental taps.
Pass short taps to the keyboard

Hold to record normally; a short tap is not recorded and is forwarded to the keyboard’s voice key underneath, so the IME’s own short-press action is not blocked by the transparent overlay. Requires the accessibility gesture permission; turn the accessibility service off and on after updating.

Tap “Calibrate position” to show a blue dashed target above the keyboard. Adjust width and height separately, drag it over your keyboard’s voice key, then save. Each IME/orientation gets its own profile.
One word per line, or wrong=>correct
A bare word is sent to the server as recognition context. Rules with => replace text locally. A re: prefix means regular expression, e.g. re:helo=>hello.
All IME positions and sizes were reset
Tap here to open the keyboard, then hold the transparent target

1. Start the CapsWriter-Offline server on your computer and keep phone and computer on the same LAN.
2. Enter the computer’s LAN IP and port, then save and test.
3. Grant microphone and notification permissions, and enable the accessibility service.
4. Turn on “Enable floating voice input” and calibrate the target over your keyboard’s voice key.
5. In any app, open the keyboard, hold the transparent area, speak, and release. The text is inserted into the focused field.

The app is hidden from the recent tasks list by default; return via the notification or the launcher icon.
If an app rejects accessibility text insertion, the result is copied to the clipboard.
